atlas-pl.0117: The employer must state the pay or range in the advert, before the interview or before the contract; we found no page on negotiation norms, a thirteenth month or the time to decide.
atlas-pl.0118: A non-EU hire normally needs a Type A work permit from the voivode, preceded by a labour-market test (the district office’s information, 14 to 21 days) unless the occupation is on the regional shortage list; the employer pays PLN 400 for contracts over three months.
atlas-pl.0119: Two shortcuts exist: the EU Blue Card needs a salary of at least PLN 13,355.34 gross a month in 2026, far above entry pay, while a graduate of a Polish full-time course is permanently exempt from permits. A foreign student on a full-time course can work without a permit during the degree.
atlas-pl.0120: Raise it at the first interview; centres used to foreign staff will know the process, others will think of the labour-market test. EU and EEA citizens need no permit.
atlas-pl.0121: Portals: Just Join IT for tech, the Civil Service board for public posts, the public employment services’ Zielona Linia; career pages of PKO Bank Polski, KPMG, EY, PwC and Deloitte for students and graduates.
atlas-pl.0122: Fairs and career offices: the University of Warsaw Career Office lists faculty fairs and career days; KPMG’s World of Audit workshops are held in October.
atlas-pl.0123: Business-services centres hire in volume by language; their employers are listed by ABSL, the sector association.
atlas-pl.0124: Leaving the data-processing clause (klauzula RODO) off the CV, which many recruiters expect.
atlas-pl.0125: Missing the programme window: KPMG’s workshops are three dates in October and its recruitment has ended for this year; PwC’s summer programme is closed for 2026 and starts again in July.
atlas-pl.0126: Treating the centres as safe: automation runs in more than 74% of them and the junior share is falling.
atlas-pl.0127: Relying on old intake figures: the 100 to 200 interns per Big Four firm quoted in the press date from 2010.
atlas-pl.0128: Answering a question about your past salary: since the 2025 amendment an employer may not ask for it.
atlas-pl.0129: Western banks’ centres work in English with a second European language as a paid extra; local banks such as PKO recruit in Polish (its pages are in Polish).
atlas-pl.0130: KPMG asks for very good English for its audit internship and tests English online; the Big Four’s client work is in Polish. No page states a certificate level.
atlas-pl.0131: In the service centres English is the working language and a second language earns an allowance of PLN 600 to 2,000 a month; foreigners are 19.6% of staff.
atlas-pl.0132: Tech firms and the Just Join IT board work largely in English, which is why 668 of 19,988 offers are junior and the competition is international; no language certificate is mentioned on the pages we read.
atlas-pl.0133: Civil-service posts are advertised in Polish and the board has a filter for offers open to foreigners; we found no page stating a Polish level.
atlas-pl.0134: In 2025, 91.2% of Polish tertiary graduates aged 20–34 who finished within the last three years were in work (EU 85.3%), and unemployment among 15-to-24-year-olds was 12.2% (EU 15.2%).
atlas-pl.0135: PKO says over 60% of its interns continue working with the bank; Warsaw University of Technology says 44% of its graduates had a job before graduating. We found no national conversion rate for internships.
atlas-pl.0136: EU, EEA and Swiss citizens work with no authorisation.
atlas-pl.0137: Staying over three months, register your stay at the voivode’s office by the day after the three months end; the certificate is free.
atlas-pl.0138: Register your address (meldunek) at the town hall within 30 days of moving in; it gives you a PESEL number at no cost.
atlas-pl.0139: Student visa and temporary residence permit
atlas-pl.0140: Get the national student visa (D09) at a consulate; the first residence permit lasts 15 months and is applied for online on the MOS portal, where the university signs its part.
atlas-pl.0141: Full-time (stationary) students may work without limit and with no work permit; part-time or weekend students need one.
atlas-pl.0142: A non-EU student with a permit from another EU country in an EU programme needs no Polish visa or permit for up to 360 days, after the university notifies the Border Guard.
atlas-pl.0148: For graduates of the last two years or students outside the EU, with a written traineeship contract at a host approved by the interior ministry; up to six months, renewable once.
atlas-pl.0149: Full-time students in Poland can do internships with no permit.
atlas-pl.0150: Permit for graduates of Polish universities
atlas-pl.0151: After a degree or doctorate in Poland, apply while still lawfully resident: nine months, once, to find work or start a business.
atlas-pl.0152: Graduates of full-time Polish programmes are exempt from work permits for life: any employer can hire them directly, with no labour-market test.
atlas-pl.0154: A contract of at least six months and a three-year degree, or five years of experience (three in the last seven for IT and managers); no labour-market test, and a spouse may work at once. Apply online through MOS.
atlas-pl.0158: Single permit to stay and work
atlas-pl.0159: The employer first gets a work permit from the voivode, usually after a labour-market test by the job centre, then you get a D visa and apply for the single permit online before the visa runs out.
atlas-pl.0160: €135 visa; PLN 440 + PLN 100 card; employer PLN 400
atlas-pl.0162: A master’s degree and a hosting agreement with a research body approved by the science ministry; no work permit is needed for the project.
atlas-pl.0163: Doctoral-school students receive a stipend free of income tax but with pension contributions, and need no work permit.
atlas-pl.0165: PLN 3,570.50 gross a month for the first two years, PLN 5,500.50 after
atlas-pl.0166: Poland has working-holiday agreements only with New Zealand, Australia, Canada, Japan, Taiwan, South Korea, Chile and Argentina.
atlas-pl.0167: For citizens of those countries aged 18 to 30 (35 for Canada): a 12-month D visa with work allowed and no permit, usually not convertible inside Poland.
atlas-pl.0168: Up to 90 days in any 180; work only with an authorisation obtained before you start.
atlas-pl.0169: Nothing to arrange in advance: work is open to you, and registration is needed only if you stay more than 3 months.
atlas-pl.0170: Since 27 April 2026 every residence application goes through the MOS portal (mos.cudzoziemcy.gov.pl), signed with a Trusted Profile; paper applications are set aside unexamined. For a work permit, your employer completes and signs its annex from a link MOS sends.
atlas-pl.0171: Register your address (zameldowanie) at the local municipal office within 30 days of moving in, with passport or ID, residence document or visa, and a lease signed by the owner; EU citizens must once they stay over 3 months, others once they stay over 30 days. It is free; a paper certificate costs 21 PLN.
atlas-pl.0172: Staying over 3 months, register your stay at the voivode’s office by the day after the 3 months end; students bring enrolment, a statement of means and the European Health Insurance Card. The paper certificate is free and valid 10 years.
atlas-pl.0173: Attend the voivode’s appointment for fingerprints; once the decision is positive, pay 100 PLN to collect the residence card. The stamp duty for the application is 440 PLN for work and 340 PLN for study or research.
atlas-pl.0174: The 11-digit PESEL number, needed for tax, work contracts, public health care and digital ID, is given free when you register your address; without a lease yet, you can ask for it for tax purposes.
atlas-pl.0175: Your employer must register you with ZUS within 7 days of hiring, which brings public health cover (NFZ). Students under 26 on a civil-law contract (zlecenie) pay no ZUS or income tax.
atlas-pl.0176: Students and trainees without a job use the European Health Insurance Card.
atlas-pl.0177: Students without cover take private insurance of at least €30,000, or voluntary NFZ insurance at about 55.80 PLN a month for foreign students.
atlas-pl.0178: Activate the Trusted Profile (Profil Zaufany), the state’s digital ID and e-signature, in two minutes through a Polish bank (mBank, PKO BP, Santander, Pekao, Millennium, ING, Alior), or online at pz.gov.pl with a check in person at a tax office, ZUS or the voivode’s office. It is free.
atlas-pl.0180: File for a new permit by the last day of your legal stay: you then stay legally until the decision, but may work only if you already could, or are renewing a single permit with the same employer and job.
atlas-pl.0181: The MOS certificate or the voivode’s stamp is not a travel document: you may leave by a direct route home, but cannot return with it, and must not travel in Schengen once your visa or visa-free days run out.
atlas-pl.0182: Since 27 April 2026 residence applications are accepted only online through MOS, which needs a Trusted Profile (Profil Zaufany); paper applications are dismissed.
